heading: Few parameters and few dependencies
body:
A long list of parameters hides a missing model: the values belong together, but the code passes them one by one. A class that needs many other classes does more than one job.

So a method takes at most 4 parameters. When it needs more, put the values that belong together in a model, a class in `client/models` or `server/models`, and take that model as one parameter. These do not count:

`self`, `this` and `cls`.

A parameter that Tachyon fills from the request: `FromPath`, `FromQuery`, `FromBody`, `FromHeader` and `FromCookie`. Each one names one part of the request.

The parameters of a constructor. The next rule covers them.

A class needs at most 5 other classes. The classes it needs are the ones it names (see Dependencies point down), plus the `DataSource`, `Redis` and `ApplicationEventPublisher` resources. When a class needs more, split it into smaller classes that each need fewer, and let each caller use the part it needs.

The build refuses either problem with `TY1329`, for example: The method `place` in OrderService takes 5 parameters; the limit is 4.

This check is new, so you can turn it off for one side of the app while you move code. For Tac code, set `tac.signatures.check` to `false` in `client/manifest.json`. For Yon code, set `signatures.check` to `false` in `server/application.json`. Use these settings only for migration. `ty migrate check` lists every place to change, even when the setting is off.
